title: Springboard: company sprint communique and all-hands plan
content:
Purpose and context
---
This doc is the working communique for the Springboard planning window: a short-cycle company-wide planning + all-hands that (a) resets top-level OKRs for the next 6–8 weeks, (b) provides exec-level context for customers/partners, and (c) aligns go-to-market asks and cross-functional owners. Treat this as a living draft — expect lots of inline TODOs and open questions.

High-level intent (one-liner)
---
Make the next quarter feel like a momentum burst: tighten 3 company-level outcomes, surface visible wins for customers, and reduce ambiguity for product/eng teams so we can execute faster.

Priority outcomes we want from the springboard window (internal framing)
---
- Outcome A: Reduce median host-api p99 latency by 20% for typical chat workloads while keeping unit cost <= current baseline. (Why: product reliability + cost story for GTM).
- Outcome B: Launch Redwood Dedicated rollout playbook + 2 pilot customers onboarded to Dedicated. (Why: revenue/enterprise motion).
- Outcome C: Improve quality regression detection pipeline: integrate 10 prompt test cases into auto-evals + alerting. (Why: reduce customer regression risk during model rollouts).

Draft company OKRs (top-level) — iterate in review
---
OKR 1 — Production economics (owner: VP Eng, serving runtime)
- KR1.1: Median p99 generation latency for hosted chat (8k tokens traffic slice) down 20% from baseline (baseline collected 2026-02-01).
- KR1.2: Average per-token spend for production gen calls down 12% via batching + cache heuristics enabled on 60% of traffic.
- KR1.3: Deployment success rate (canary->prod) >= 99% (failed deploy rollback latency < 5 minutes).

OKR 2 — Enterprise motion (owner: Head of Sales + Product)
- KR2.1: 2 Dedicated pilot customers onboarded and on a 6mo purchase path (MOU signed).
- KR2.2: Dedicated readiness checklist fully documented + 3 runbook drills executed (SRE + Solutions ENG).
- KR2.3: Security/compliance checklist (SOC-like) initial gap closure >= 75% for target pilot customers.

OKR 3 — Model quality guardrails (owner: Research/Applied ML)
- KR3.1: Auto-eval pipeline integrated into the deployment flow for at least 3 models; weekly regression alerts enabled.
- KR3.2: Rolling baseline created from production prompts (at least 10k anonymized queries) with automated drift detection.
- KR3.3: False-positive rate for quality alerts < 10% after two tuning iterations.

Notes on KRs: these are intentionally short-cycle, measurable and tied to existing efforts (batching, Dedicated playbook, eval infra). Feedback requested on targets and owners.

All-hands run-of-show (proposed) — 60 minutes total
---
0–5m: Welcome + quick one-liner framing (CEO)
5–20m: State of the ship — short exec updates (product, eng, go-to-market) with numbers vs baseline (each 3–4 minutes)
20–35m: Springboard OKR narrative — why these outcomes, owners, and how teams will operate during the cycle (VPs + product leads)
35–45m: Customer spotlight (pilot customer story / case study) — prerecorded video + 1 live Q&A (if available)
45–55m: Team weekly cadence and how to escalate blockers (demo of new dashboards + how to submit a 'stop the ship' flag)
55–60m: Asks, quick polls, closing + next steps (eng/ops owners call out immediate actions)

Slide asks (what we need from teams to fill slides)
---
- Product: 1 slide per OKR with current baseline, why it matters, top 3 activities, and owner contact. (due: 2026-02-28)
- Eng: 2 slides — 1 pager on latency/cost plan (what will change), and one on rollout safeguards. (due: 2026-03-03)
- GTM: 1 slide per pilot customer with commercial/technical status (due: 2026-03-03)
- Research/Quality: demo slide of the auto-eval pipeline and 2 sample prompt tests (due: 2026-03-03)

Communication plan & channels
---
- Pre-read (24–48 hours before): short doc + 2–3 slides shared to #all and the home page of Console.
- Live event: record, publish recording + timestamped highlights (product, eng, asks) in Confluence.
- Post-event: one-pager with actions and owners in the company ops tracker (GH issue and Confluence)

Immediate asks for execs (for the next 10 days)
---
- Product: finalize OKR phrasing + signoff on KRs by 2026-03-02.
- Eng SRE: confirm runbook for Dedicated pilot failover by 2026-03-04.
- Research: push first 10 prompt tests into eval infra; tag as "springboard-primary" by 2026-03-04.
- GTM: confirm customer readiness checklist and initial comms plan by 2026-03-06.

Risk heatmap (quick, working)
---
1) Pilot customer readiness — Likelihood: medium-high; Impact: high. Mitigation: triage weekly, provide SRE seat, prepare fallback to hosted offering. Owner: Solutions Eng.
2) Latency optimization regressions — Likelihood: medium; Impact: medium-high. Mitigation: canary ramp controls + auto rollback, heavy perf testing. Owner: Serving runtime.
3) Auto-eval false positives — Likelihood: medium; Impact: medium. Mitigation: filter tuning + human-in-loop review for first 2 weeks. Owner: Research.
4) Communication confusion across orgs — Likelihood: high; Impact: medium. Mitigation: single source-of-truth pre-read + designated comms owner. Owner: Company Ops.

Decision log (open)
---
- D1: OKR cadence length — do we make these 6-week sprint OKRs or 8-week? (open)
- D2: Public-facing vs internal story for latency improvements (open — marketing ask to soften numbers)
- D3: Which pilot gets first Dedicated billing arrangement (open — prioritize customer with infra readiness)

Open questions / things to resolve in the next sync
---
- Q1: Are the latency targets realistic without major infra spend? Need numbers from infra finance. (Assigned: Infra Finance | due 2026-03-01)
- Q2: How to handle sensitive customer quotes in the Customer Spotlight? (Assigned: Legal + CSMs | due 2026-03-03)
- Q3: Who will be the single comms lead for the pre-read and the Confluence publish? (Assigned: Ops)

Execution timeline (compact)
---
- 2026-02-20: Draft created (this doc)
- 2026-02-24: Leadership review + edits (async)
- 2026-03-02: Final OKR signoff deadline
- 2026-03-04: Slides due from eng/product/GTM
- 2026-03-08: Dry run + recording test (presenters in place)
- 2026-03-10: All-hands day (record + publish)
- 2026-03-11–25: Post-mortem + sprint kickoff for teams aligned to OKRs

Quick checklist for owners (copyable)
---
- [ ] Confirm slide owner and slack channel (deadline)
- [ ] Link supporting artifacts (Jira tickets, Confluence pages) in slide notes
- [ ] Ensure runbook pages link into SRE oncall (for Dedicated pilot)
- [ ] Tag any external SHAs or model IDs used in evals for reproducibility

Notes to self / draft friction points (honest, rough)
---
- We need to avoid "vague marketing spin" — the engineering team wants explicit numbers. But marketing wants simpler customer-facing messaging. This will require a two-track slide set (internal vs public) — keep costs low by reusing core data.
- Solutions Eng flagged that Dedicated pilot requires a DR checklist we don't yet have. Short-term: borrow hosted DR pattern, adapt to Dedicated constraints.
- Risk: too many owners sign up and nobody owns follow-ups. We need one person per KR who is allowed to nudge.

- Dedicated playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/DED/Dedicated+Playbook+Draft

Next steps (clear asks for owner)
---
- Avery: consolidate slides and publish pre-read by 2026-03-08 (owner: Avery Chen)
- Riley: collect OKR confirmations from VPs and update this doc (owner: Riley Patel)
- Jordan: prepare demo recording + coordinate customer consent (owner: Jordan Morales)

End of draft.
